title: This Black Friday, your AI chief of staff is 20% off
excerpt: This article is sponsored by Plaud.
content_html:
Published Nov 25, 2026, 3:03 PM EST

The below articles are sponsored by one of our partners. Product choices and opinions expressed are from the sponsor and do not reflect the views of the Android Police editorial staff.

If you ever left a meeting and realized you never wrote down a key action item, you know how unreliable memory can be. Taking notes by hand means splitting your attention between the person talking and the page, and something usually gets forgotten.

That's where Plaud comes in. The company makes AI notetakers, which are small recorders that capture conversations and use AI to transcribe and summarize them. These devices are built for conversations that happen away from the screen, which is where software-only notetakers fall short.

Through November 30, 2026, Plaud's entire notetaker lineup is 20% off at plaud.ai in the US and Canada as part of its Black Friday sale. Below is a rundown of the four models, what the AI does with your recordings, and what the sale prices look like.

The problem with manual notetaking

Software-only notetakers live on a screen, which is a poor fit for a physical boardroom, a walk between appointments, or a phone call. A dedicated device lets you focus on the person in front of you while the AI handles transcription and organization.

Used by over three million professionals every day, Plaud’s product lineup can be split into two categories: those looking to keep notes during meetings and calls, and those on the move and in the field.

Plaud Note Pro: A recorder built for the office

Plaud Note Pro

Brand
Plaud

Bluetooth
Yes

Wi-Fi
2.4GHz, 5GHz

Weight
1.05oz

Dimensions
85.6×54.1×2.99mm

Storage
64GB

The Plaud Note Pro is a credit-card-sized AI note taker with a 0.95-inch AMOLED display and smart dual-mode recording that switches between phone calls and in-person conversations. It has four MEMS microphones with 16.4 ft pickup, up to 50 hours of recording, and 64GB of storage.

If calls make up much of your day, the Plaud Note Pro is designed around your phone. It magnetically clips to the back of a phone with the included MagSafe case or sits flat on a table, so it's on hand whether you're on a call or in a meeting. The recorder detects in-person conversations and phone calls, while Plaud Desktop covers online meetings.

On calls, the Note Pro captures both sides of the conversation by picking up the phone speaker’s vibration, so both voices end up in the recording. And in person, four microphones pick up voices from up to 16.4 feet away.

The Note Pro is 0.12 inches thick and weighs 1.06 oz. A 0.95-inch screen shows recording status and battery level, so you can check on it at a glance.

Battery life runs up to 30 hours in Enhance mode or up to 50 hours in Endurance mode, and the device has 64 GB of storage. The box includes a free black magnetic case, a magnetic ring, and a charging cable.

Typically $189.00, the Note Pro is $149.99 through November 30th as part of the 20% Black Friday sale. The Plaud Note is available for $126.99.

Plaud NotePin S: A wearable for those on the move

Plaud NotePin S

Weight
0.61 oz

Dimensions
2.01 × 0.83 × 0.43 in

Storage
64GB

Connectivity
BLE 5.2, Wi-Fi

Charging
2 hours

Recording time
Up to 20 hours continuous, up to 40 days standby

The Plaud NotePin S is a wearable AI note taker with a tactile record button and a Press to Highlight feature, and four wearable accessories in the box. It weighs 0.61 oz, records for up to 20 hours, and picks up voices from up to 9.84 feet away.

If you're on your feet more than at a desk, the Plaud NotePin S is made to be worn. You can clip it to a shirt, wrap it around your wrist, or wear it around your neck as a lanyard, and starting a recording takes a single press.

While you record, an instant-highlight button flags moments in real time. That helps when someone mentions a deadline or a specific requirement that you'll want to find quickly later. Afterward, you get a full transcript, your highlights, and a structured summary.

The NotePin S was named to TIME's Best Inventions of 2026, and currently costs only $142.99, while the Plaud NotePin is available for $126.99.

AI tools that organize your knowledge

Plaud’s AI transcribes in 112 languages and identifies speakers, so you don't have to work out who said what in a group meeting. Summaries are structured around key concepts and follow-up questions, and on the Note Pro, they also cover key decisions and action items.

Ask Plaud searches across all your recordings and notes, pulls quotes, and reformats summaries. This means you can look up what was said without replaying the audio. The resulting notes turn into a searchable knowledge base that grows with every recording.

You can then take your notes to the next level with the use of Plaud Agent, which turns conversations into emails, reports, presentations, and spreadsheets. Plus, with integrations with Google Calendar, Slack, Notion, and Linear, you can integrate the results with your current workflow.

Privacy and compliance for regulated industries

Privacy is at the forefront with Plaud, making it perfect for attorneys, HR, and consultants with regulated work. Recordings and transcripts aren't shared with third parties or accessed without permission, and everything is encrypted in transit and at rest.

Plaud is HIPAA, SOC 2 Type 2, EN 18031, and GDPR compliant, and full local data processing is an option.

Which Plaud device fits your workflow?

If your day is mostly phone calls and office meetings, the Plaud Note and Note Pro's MagSafe case and call capture fit that routine. If you're often on your feet or in the field, the NotePin S and NotePin's clip, wrist, and lanyard options suit it better.

Every model comes with the free Starter plan, so the AI features and 300 monthly minutes are included whichever one you pick.

The Black Friday discounts run through November 30th at plaud.ai in the U.S. and Canada. If you want your meetings to leave behind something searchable instead of something you have to remember, now's a good time to consider checking out one of these AI recorders.
